card.name: Bagurumba
card.tagline: The Bodo 'butterfly dance' mirroring nature's grace
card.profile: Bagurumba is a traditional dance of the indigenous Bodo (Boro) people of Assam, nicknamed the 'butterfly dance' because its slow, poised movements imitate butterflies, birds and swaying flowers (Wikipedia). Performed mainly by women during the spring festival Bwishagu (mid-April), dancers wear the colourful handwoven dokhona, jwmgra (fasra) and aronai, using the jwmgra cloth like butterfly wings. It is accompanied by instruments including the sifung (long bamboo flute), serja (bowed instrument), kham (drum), jota and gongwna (Wikipedia; The Better India).
card.insight: At 'Bagurumba Dwhou 2026', held 17 January 2026 in Guwahati, over 10,000 artistes - including roughly 8,000 dancers drawn from 81 assembly constituencies across 23 districts - performed together (The Meghalayan Express; narendramodi.in).
